title: Dereferencing and Null Pointers
learningObjectives: Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: Dereferencing a valid pointer accesses the object it points to. A null pointer represents no valid object; dereferencing null is undefined behavior.
understand.whyItMatters: Null checks and indirect access help avoid crashes and undefined behavior.
understand.explain: Use nullptr for an empty pointer and check before dereference when null is possible.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Dereferencing and Null Pointers examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing dereferencing and null pointers. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.
